correction.text: the prefecture of Mysore, 1399: no extent on any page opened

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, 1399-1571: Cliopatria's Mysore row begins in 1572. The Wadiyar page has Yaduraya made prefect of Mysore 'in 1399' under Harihara II and the Kingdom of Mysore page 'Established: 1399' and the earliest Wodeyar inscription dated to 1551; neither gives an extent, so a 25 km radius round Mysore is a placeholder (low confidence). The Wodeyars were Vijayanagara's feudatories, not independent, until the 1565 collapse; the kingdom page has them stop sending tribute to Chandragiri only by 1612-13. [Repair sa-05-b, 2026-10-25] Mysore is a Vijayanagara vassal from 1399 to 1613 (ledger vassal_start and vassal_end); the shape is the vassal's own land.

The Treaty of Seringapatam page then shows what Tipu held in 1791: the Malabar Coast between Travancore and the Kali River, the Baramahal and Dindigul districts, land from the Krishna River to the Penner River with Cuddapah and Gandikota, and the country up to the Tungabhadra. [Repair sa-05-b, 2026-10-25] Mysore is still a Vijayanagara tributary in 1572 (vassal_end 1613); this event moves the land of the drawn Mysore country from the empire's outline (vijayanagara-empire's 1572 loss) to Mysore's, it does not end the tribute.

region.text: the Mysore country, as Cliopatria draws it from 1572, with Srirangapatna

ledger.note: 1613: the Wodeyars stop paying tribute to Vijayanagara's seat. Kingdom of Mysore page (reopened 2026-10-25): 'by 1612-13, the Wodeyars exercised a great deal of autonomy' and 'tributes and transfers of revenue to Chandragiri stopped'. The pages disagree on the date: the Wadiyar page has the vassalage 'until around 1553', says Mysore became independent after the breakup of 1565 (the Kingdom page infobox: 'Independent state (1565-1799)') and has the Wadiyars 'declared independence' with the seizure of Srirangapattana in 1610. 1613 is the year of the one sentence that dates the end of the tribute (reviewer sa-05-b asked for 1572 or 1612-13). The vijayanagara-empire dossier has no vassal event for Mysore and loses the Mysore country in 1572.

ledger.note: 1673: Chikka Devaraja takes the throne (28 February 1673) and Cliopatria draws his whole reign's conquests from this year. The Kingdom page has him adding Salem and Bangalore to the east and Hassan to the west, and taking Chikkamagaluru, Tumkur and the rest of Coimbatore; the Chikka Devaraja page has Maddagiri and 'the regions around Baramahal and Salem below the Eastern Ghats'; none is dated, so the year is a bridge over 1673-1704. [Repair sa-05-b, 2026-10-25] Coimbatore is split out into its own 1673 gain against nayaks-of-madurai (reviewer sa-05-b).

Kingdom of Mysore page (reopened 2026-10-25): under Chikka Devaraja the kingdom grew to include 'the rest of Coimbatore to the south'; the page gives no year and no former holder. The nayaks-of-madurai dossier holds Coimbatore (Thirumalai Nayak page) and records the matching loss in 1673, also at confidence 1.

region.text: Bangalore

ledger.note: 1687: Chikka Devaraja gets Bangalore. He agreed to buy it from Venkoji 'for three lakh rupees', but the Mughal army under Khasim Khan occupied it and 'hoisted the Mughal flag on its rampart on July 10, 1687'; the payment was made to Qasim Khan, the Mughal faujdar of Sira. The page gives no date for the sale.

ledger.note: 1700: Chikka Devaraja sends an embassy to Aurangzeb and receives 'a formal subordination to Mughal authority and a requirement to pay annual tribute' (Chikka Devaraja page, reopened 2026-10-25). The Kingdom of Mysore page has Mysore 'now formally a tributary of the Mughal Empire' (two historians; 'Mughul records claim a regular tribute (peshkash) was paid') while another historian 'feels the Mughals may have considered Mysore an ally'. Confidence 2: the year is the page's, the nature of the tie is disputed. Reviewer sa-05-b: the status was on a page opened but not in the ledger.

The Kingdom page has 'the Mughal residents at both Arcot and Sira claiming tribute' 'by the 1720s, with the Mughal empire in decline', and the mughal-empire dossier hands the Nizam's Deccan to hyderabad-state in 1724; Cliopatria's Mughal shape holds no cell within 60 km of Bengaluru from 1706 (gazetteer check). 1761: Hyder Ali becomes ruler of Mysore. 'Hyder Ali became king of Mysore in 1761' after overthrowing the prime minister (Hyder Ali page); the Kingdom page infobox lists him for 1761-1782 and Tipu Sultan for 1782-1799; the Wadiyar page keeps the Wadiyars as nominal rulers. The state, its colour and its dossier continue.

[Repair sa-05-b, 2026-10-25] Bellary is added: it lies in the strip between the Tungabhadra and the Penner, the Ceded Districts page (reopened) says Tipu 'agreed to give his northern territory to the Nizam of Hyderabad in 1792' and lists Bellary among the districts the Nizam ceded to the Company in 1800, and the 1799 partition (Fourth Anglo-Mysore War and Ceded Districts pages) names no Bellary. Confidence 3 to 2: neither the Treaty page nor the Ceded Districts page names Bellary for 1792. This differs from the reviewer's suggestion to keep Bellary with Mysore until 1799; see the notes.

region.text: Coimbatore and Dakshina Kannada

ledger.note: 1799: after Seringapatam falls on 4 May 1799, Mysore 'ceded Coimbatore and Dakshina Kannada to the British'. The page gives no day for the cession.

4 May 1799: Tipu falls at Seringapatam and the British restore Mysore to the Wadiyars. The page: the victors 'restored control of Mysore to the Wadiyars' under indirect British control, with a commissioner; Krishnaraja III is a child (five years old on the Kingdom page, four on the Wadiyar page). The dossier continues as the princely state.
1799: the capital returns from Srirangapatna to Mysore. Wadiyar page: after 1799 the capital was moved back to Mysore.

1831: the British take direct control of Mysore. The Wadiyar page puts the kingdom under the Mysore Commission from 1831 to 1881; the Kingdom page has the British taking direct control in 1831. Colour and dossier continue.
1834: Mark Cubbon, Commissioner from 1834, makes Bangalore the capital.
1881: power returns to the Wadiyars. The Wadiyar page has power transferred back to the Wadiyars; the Kingdom page has Chamaraja X restored in 1881.

region.text: Mysore as the Wadiyars held it after 1799

ledger.note: 9 August 1947: Mysore joins the Indian Union. The Kingdom of Mysore text has Mysore joining the Indian Union on 9 August 1947 (the infobox has 1950, and the Wadiyar page has the Maharaja remaining until the republic in 1950).

wars.name: Bijapur's repulse of Mysore (siege of Srirangapatna, 1638)
wars.outcome: Chamaraja VI and Kanthirava Narasaraja I tried to expand north; Bijapur repelled them and the 1638 siege of Srirangapatna failed.
wars.note: Title is descriptive; the page gives the repulse and the siege, not a named war.

wars.name: Chikka Devaraja's Trichinopoly campaign
wars.outcome: In 1696 Chikka Devaraja attacked the Nayaks of Madura and besieged Trichinopoly; 'the siege of Trichnopoly had to be abandoned because the alliance had begun to rupture' (no date on the page). No ground was held.
wars.note: The end year 1697 is a bridge.

wars.name: First Anglo-Mysore War
wars.outcome: Began in August 1767 with the attack on the Company outpost at Changama; Hyder reached within five miles of Madras and sued for peace. The Treaty of Madras of 29 March 1769 restored the status quo except for Mysore's acquisition of Karur.
wars.note: The Kingdom page has the British allied with the Marathas and the Nizam.

wars.name: Maratha invasion of Mysore (Madhavrao's third war against Hyder)

intersect.text: the north-east of Mysore up to Bangalore

zones.text: 'much of north-eastern Mysore' and the land 'all the way to Bangalore' (Hyder Ali page): the Cliopatria shape within 45 km of Bengaluru, 55 km of Tumakuru and 50 km of Kolar, about 16,400 km2; my reading, the page names no town

wars.outcome: The Marathas invaded in November 1770 with 35,000 men, took much of north-eastern Mysore and Bangalore; Hyder sued for peace in 1772, paid 3.6 million rupees of arrears and 1.4 million a year, and ceded territory all the way to Bangalore; Tipu was sent to recover it in 1773.
wars.note: The Kingdom of Mysore page counts three wars between Madhavrao I and Hyder 'from 1764 and 1772'; only the invasion of November 1770 and the peace of 1772 are detailed on the Hyder Ali page.

wars.name: Second Anglo-Mysore War
wars.outcome: Hyder won at Pollilur (10 September 1780 on the Hyder Ali page, 27 August 1781 on the Kingdom page) and lost at Porto Novo; he died on 7 December 1782 and Tipu succeeded him. The Treaty of Mangalore (1784) restored the lands to their prior state.

wars.name: Maratha-Mysore War
wars.outcome: Ended in a peace agreement after Tipu's victory at Bahadur Benda; the terms are not on the page (the infobox says 1759-1787, the text 1785-1787).

wars.name: Third Anglo-Mysore War

zones.text: the country up to the Tungabhadra
the land from the Krishna to the Penner River, with the forts of Cuddapah and Gandikota

union.text: the Malabar coast north of Kozhikode

zones.text: the Malabar Coast, the Baramahal and Dindigul

wars.outcome: Began after Tipu attacked Travancore; the Treaty of Seringapatam of 18 March 1792 took about one-half of Mysore for the British, the Nizam and the Marathas and left two of Tipu's sons as hostages.

wars.name: Fourth Anglo-Mysore War
wars.outcome: The fort of Seringapatam was stormed on 4 May 1799 and Tipu killed; the Wadiyars were restored in a subsidiary alliance, ceding Coimbatore and Dakshina Kannada to the British.
wars.note: The page names no division of the rest between the British, the Nizam and the Marathas beyond Savanur.

certainty.note: No page opened gives a boundary line; the Chikka Devaraja extent is a list of places (Medigeshi to Palni and Anaimalai) and the Hyder-era extent a river-and-ghats description ('bordered by the Krishna River in the north').

The 1792 treaty cedes named districts and territory up to the Tungabhadra River; the 1799 settlement names Coimbatore and Dakshina Kannada; the princely state's later boundaries are on no page opened and are taken as administrative lines.

sources.title: Kingdom of Mysore
sources.note: Identity, the 205,000 km2 of 1779, Hyder and Tipu, the Anglo-Mysore wars, 1799, 1831, 1881, 1947. The early expansion has no dates.

sources.title: Wadiyar dynasty
sources.note: Yaduraya 1399, capital moves (Srirangapatna 1610, back to Mysore after 1799), Mysore Commission 1831-1881, 1947. A sixth page, one over the budget of five, opened for the capitals and the founding.

sources.title: Chikka Devaraja
sources.note: 28 February 1673, Bangalore 1687, the west to the Baba Budan Mountains 1694, Trichinopoly 1696, 1700, extent at death in 1704.

sources.title: Hyder Ali
sources.note: Rise 1755-1761, Keladi 1763, Kozhikode 1766, the First and Second Anglo-Mysore Wars, death in December 1782.

sources.title: Treaty of Seringapatam
sources.note: 18 March 1792: the cessions to the British, the Nizam and the Marathas, Coorg.

sources.title: Fourth Anglo-Mysore War
sources.note: 4 May 1799, the restoration of the Wadiyars, Coimbatore and Dakshina Kannada ceded. Thin on the settlement.

sources.title: Ceded Districts
sources.note: Repair of sa-05-b: 'Tippu Sultan agreed to give his northern territory to the Nizam of Hyderabad in 1792'; the Ceded Districts (Bellary among them) 'ceded' by the Nizam to the Company in 1800; the Mysore territories 'divided up among the Wodeyars, the Nizam and the British' after 1799. No year for Bellary's transfer.

notes:
Cliopatria row 'Kingdom of Mysore' 1572-1799 (5 shapes, 18,135 to 91,042 km2). The dossier runs from 1399 (Wadiyar page: Yaduraya prefect of Mysore) to 9 August 1947 (Mysore joins the Indian Union), because the princely state is the same Wadiyar kingdom and no other dossier covers 1800-1947; if the orchestrator prefers Cliopatria's span, cut at 1799 and drop the 1800 keyframe and the 1831-1947 events. The Hyder Ali and Tipu Sultan period is one state under 'rename' events (1761, 1782, 1799); a 'Sultanate of Mysore' split would need the cut at 1761 and 1799.
Cliopatria problems: (1) the 1673 shape (91,042 km2) is the extent at Chikka Devaraja's death in 1704, drawn 31 years early; (2) the 1709 shape stays at 91,000 km2 through Hyder's and Tipu's expansion although the page gives 205,000 km2 for 1779 (ratio 0.44); three new keyframes (1763, 1766, 1779) correct it, and the union of the 1779 keyframe resolves to about 206,000 km2; (3) the 1799 shape keeps Coimbatore and Dakshina Kannada, ceded that year; (4) Srirangapatna is inside the 1572 shape although it was taken in 1610; (5) the row starts 1572, the page 1399, and the Wodeyars paid tribute to Chandragiri to 1612-13.
Page silent or in conflict: Chikka Devaraja's accession 1672 (Cliopatria, Kingdom page) or 28 February 1673 (his page); the early conquests (Satyamangalam, Erode, Dharmapuri, Maddagiri, Salem, Baramahal, Hassan, Chikmagalur, Tumkur, Coimbatore) have no dates; who took Srirangapatna in 1610 (Raja Wodeyar I or Timmaraja Wodeyar II); Pollilur 10 September 1780 (Hyder Ali page) or 27 August 1781 (Kingdom page); Hyder's accession 1761 against 'between 1766 and 1799' for nominal Wadiyar rule on the Wadiyar page; Krishnaraja III aged four or five; the 1784 and 1787 treaties give no territorial terms (the 1772 peace does: 'ceded territory all the way to Bangalore', Hyder Ali page, now in the ledger); when Mysore took Cuddapah, Kurnool, Anantapur, Dindigul and the Baramahal is on no page opened (drawn from 1779 at confidence 1-2); Karur's former holder; the 1799 division of the rest between the Nizam, the Marathas and the British; the Mughal tributary status from 1700 ('formally a tributary' against 'an ally') is now drawn 1700-1724 with a bridged end (see the repair paragraph); the 1696 Trichinopoly siege moved no border. Pages opened: 6 (budget 5): Kingdom of Mysore, Wadiyar dynasty, Chikka Devaraja, Hyder Ali, Treaty of Seringapatam, Fourth Anglo-Mysore War. No ruler strip: no page opened lists the reigns.
Counterparts: vijayanagara-empire (its dossier records the matching loss in 1572), mughal-empire (Bangalore 1687), hyderabad-state (1792, its dossier records the gain), maratha-empire (1777, 1792), british-empire (1769, 1792, 1799; the dossier is not yet written), republic-of-india (1947). Needing dossiers: the Nayakas of Keladi (Bednur; the vijayanagara-empire dossier already uses the name), the Zamorin of Kozhikode (Calicut), Coorg (Kodagu), the Karnataka coast chiefs, the Nawab of Savanur.
Gazetteer: Baba Budan, Cuddapah, Gandikota, Baramahal, Medigeshi, Keladi/Ikkeri, Dharwad (Hubballi is used) and Erode are not in the gazetteer (coordinates or a neighbouring place used).

REPAIR sa-05-b-fixed (2026-10-25), after the reviewer's verdict 'fail'. Pages reopened: Hyder Ali, Kingdom of Mysore, Wadiyar dynasty, Chikka Devaraja, Treaty of Seringapatam, Fourth Anglo-Mysore War (nothing on the 1799 division of Bellary), plus Ceded Districts (new, 7 pages in all against a budget of 5). Changed: (1) 1772 loss of the north-east up to Bangalore to maratha-empire, with the November 1770 invasion as contest_start/contest_end, a war entry and the 1773 recovery (confidence 1: the page gives Tipu's mission, not its result); keyframe 1766-1778 split into 1766, 1769 (Karur added from 1769), 1772, 1773 and 1778. The annual tribute of 1.4 million rupees is not drawn as a vassal tint: no duration on the page, war resumed within a year. (2) Dharwad and Bellary moved from 1766 to 1778 (confidence 1, inside the 1776-1779 conflicts of the Hyder Ali page). (3) 1792 Maratha loss cut to the Dharwad country (Hubballi 70 km). (4) vassal_start 1399 / vassal_end 1613 for Vijayanagara and vassal_start 1700 / vassal_end 1724 for the Mughals. (5) Coimbatore split out of the 1673 gain against nayaks-of-madurai. I DISAGREE with the reviewer on Bellary after 1792: the reviewer would keep Bellary with Mysore until 1799. The Treaty of Seringapatam page gives the Nizam 'land from the Krishna to the Penner River', Bellary lies between the Tungabhadra and the Penner, the Ceded Districts page has Tipu giving 'his northern territory' to the Nizam in 1792 and lists Bellary among the districts the Nizam ceded in 1800, and the hyderabad-state dossier already puts Bellary in its 1792 gain. No page names Bellary in 1792 or in the 1799 partition (Fourth Anglo-Mysore War: silent; Ceded Districts: 'divided up among the Wodeyars, the Nizam and the British', no districts), so Bellary goes to the Nizam in 1792 at confidence 2 and the Marathas get only the Dharwad country. Also disputed: the vassal_end from Vijayanagara. The Wadiyar page has the vassalage 'until around 1553' and independence after 1565, the Kingdom page infobox 'Independent state (1565-1799)', the Wadiyar introduction independence in 1610, and the Kingdom page body tribute stopped 'by 1612-13'; 1613 follows the one sentence that dates the tribute. The Mughal vassal_end 1724 is a bridge (no page ends it). Open mirrors in other dossiers (not mine to edit): vijayanagara-empire needs vassal_start 1399 / vassal_end 1613 for Mysore (and its 1572 loss describes the whole Mysore shape); maratha-empire needs the 1772 gain, the 1773 loss, the 1777 loss and the 1792 gain (Dharwad country); mughal-empire needs the 1700-1724 vassalage; nayaks-of-madurai /ledger/5 already matches the Coimbatore gain; hyderabad-state /ledger/4 already names Bellary. Not done (reviewer 'thin' items, for a gap-filler): the date of independence on the core (Timmaraja Wodeyar II page), the dates of Chikka Devaraja's conquests, when Dindigul, the Baramahal, Cuddapah, Kurnool and Anantapur were taken (Second Anglo-Mysore War page), and a ruler strip (the Wadiyar page has a family table without reign years). Karur is gained in 1769 and dropped from the 1792-1798 shape without an event: no page opened gives its fate.
